headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, but mem0 could still feed untrusted memory into whisper if manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 exposes no filesystem or MCP surface, and whisper has no clipboard or stdin/stdout bridge, so there is no default injection channel. The only plausible pathway is manual handoff of mem0-produced text into whisper-related tooling, which is unusual and limited. Both profiles lack a documented shared channel, so uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies mem0 output into a prompt or wrapper that whisper parses as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added later, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep mem0 and whisper in separate workflows.
Avoid copy-pasting model output into downstream prompts.
Use a plain-text delimiter or schema when transferring text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared handoff.
requires-engineering: add input sanitization at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 reports no data classes touched and no network egress; whisper touches audio/speech but has no read_filesystem, write_filesystem, or network egress. With no shared workspace, OAuth, or upload path documented, there is no plausible default leakage route between them. The pairwise interaction is blocked by the exposed surfaces in both profiles.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator mounts the same sensitive files into both agents, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent is wrapped by a third-party uploader, the current assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Run both agents under separate OS users.
Disable any external upload wrapper.
Audit the bridge before enabling file handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 has no documented write, shell, git, or network capabilities, while whisper explicitly lacks execute_shell, modify_git_state, write_filesystem, and spawn_subprocesses. Because neither agent can mutate the same resource in the profiles shown, there is no capability overlap that would create a write conflict. Uncertainty does not justify escalation here.
conditions: IF mem0 is wrapped with additional write or network tools, conflict risk may emerge.
IF whisper is embedded in an orchestrator that grants shared mutable state, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same job.
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write access.
Separate mutable state by process or container.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management component, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative memory, but whisper is an audio-speech model with no documented downstream action-taking authority. The pair lacks evidence that whisper automatically acts on mem0 output, so the cascade is limited to manual or orchestrated misuse. That makes the blast radius small and the pathway non-default.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds mem0 memory directly into a downstream action agent, cascading error risk increases.
IF whisper output is used as authoritative facts without verification, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any action.
Label mem0 output as unverified memory.
Do not auto-execute downstream actions from whisper transcripts.
requires-engineering: add verification checks before acting on generated text.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. mem0 touches no data classes and whisper only lists audio/speech, so there is no identified regulated-data flow to compare. Because the compliance questions are unanswered rather than conflicting, the safe verdict is none, not medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, reassess compliance.
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Check retention settings in the wrapper.
Keep regulated data out until policies are verified.
requires-engineering: add a compliance matrix for both agents.
